<b>Остаточный (небелковый) азот</b> — аз: Non-protein (residual) nitrogen is the nitrogen of everything left in the blood after the proteins are precipitated: about 14–28 mmol/L. Half of it is urea (made by the liver from ammonia); the rest is amino acids, uric acid (from purine breakdown), creatinine (from muscle creatine phosphate, produced at an almost constant rate) and a little ammonia. Nearly all of it is filtered in the renal glomerulus and leaves in the urine. Creatinine and urea are the main markers of kidney function.
<b>Почечная недостаточность</b> — ретенц: Renal failure causes retention azotemia: the glomeruli filter too little, and urea and creatinine build up in the blood (creatinine especially; it is used to estimate the glomerular filtration rate, GFR). Uric acid rises too, and potassium, phosphate and acids are retained, causing acidosis. In severe cases this is uremia, and dialysis is needed.
<b>Печёночная недостаточность</b> — пече: Liver failure: the liver cannot convert ammonia into urea, so urea falls while ammonia and amino acids rise. Ammonia is toxic to the brain, causing hepatic encephalopathy (confusion, “flapping” tremor — asterixis, coma).
<b>Распад белков</b> (голодание, тяжёлые: Protein breakdown (starvation, severe burns, fever, bleeding into the gut, glucocorticoid therapy) causes production azotemia: more urea is made; the kidneys cope, but its level still rises.
<b>Подагра</b> — мочевой кислоты больше,: Gout: there is more uric acid than can stay dissolved. Above ~420 µmol/L, monosodium urate crystals deposit in the joints (an attack of pain in the big toe) and form stones in the kidneys.
<b>Гидрокарбонатный буфер</b> — главный: The bicarbonate buffer is the main buffer of the extracellular fluid: H⁺ + HCO₃⁻ ⇄ H₂CO₃ ⇄ CO₂ + H₂O. Add acid: the red H⁺ ions are captured by bicarbonate, forming carbonic acid, which breaks down, and CO₂ is exhaled by the lungs (the bubbles). The system is open — the product leaves, so the pH barely changes. The kidneys then regenerate HCO₃⁻ and excrete H⁺ in the urine. pH = 6.1 + log([HCO₃⁻] / 0.03·pCO₂).
<b>Закрытая система</b> (крышка): CO₂ не: Closed system (lid on): CO₂ cannot escape, carbonic acid accumulates, and the same buffer holds the pH much less well. This is what happens with poor breathing: when ventilation stops, the bicarbonate buffer is almost useless. Its strength lies in its partnership with the lungs.
<b>Кислотно-основное состояние</b> крови: Acid–base balance of the blood: pH 7.35–7.45, pCO₂ 35–45 mmHg (set by breathing), HCO₃⁻ 22–26 mmol/L (set by the kidneys and metabolism). A shift in one component is partly offset by the other — compensation: the lungs change pCO₂ within minutes, the kidneys change HCO₃⁻ over 3–5 days. The diagram on the right shows the path of the (pH, HCO₃⁻) point.
<b>Метаболический ацидоз</b>: кислоты на: Metabolic acidosis: acids accumulate or HCO₃⁻ is lost — diabetic ketoacidosis, lactate in shock, renal failure, diarrhea, methanol poisoning. HCO₃⁻ falls. Compensation is rapid, deep (Kussmaul) breathing: pCO₂ falls and the pH rises toward normal.
<b>Метаболический алкалоз</b>: потеря ки: Metabolic alkalosis: loss of acid (vomiting, gastric suction) or excess base (diuretics, too much bicarbonate). HCO₃⁻ rises. Compensation: breathing slows and pCO₂ rises (only to a limited extent, because of the resulting lack of oxygen).
<b>Дыхательный ацидоз</b>: CO₂ не выводи: Respiratory acidosis: CO₂ is not removed — COPD, a severe asthma attack, respiratory depression (opioids, anesthesia), respiratory muscle weakness. pCO₂ rises. Compensation: over several days the kidneys retain HCO₃⁻ and excrete more H⁺.
<b>Дыхательный алкалоз</b>: CO₂ выдыхает: Respiratory alkalosis: too much CO₂ is exhaled — panic and hyperventilation, high altitude, fever, early aspirin poisoning. pCO₂ falls; tingling and cramps may occur (ionized calcium falls). Compensation: the kidneys excrete HCO₃⁻.
По нескольким числам из пробирки — мочев: From a few numbers from a test tube — urea, creatinine, pH and CO₂ — a doctor can see how the kidneys, liver and lungs are working.
\n <div><h2>Небелковый азот и кисло:
Non-protein nitrogen and acid–base balance

Blood non-protein (residual) nitrogen is 14–28 mmol/L: urea (~50%), amino acids (~25%), uric acid, creatine and creatinine, ammonia, bilirubin, indican. Azotemia can be retention azotemia (the kidneys fail to excrete) or production azotemia (too much is formed).

Blood buffer systems

  • Bicarbonate (HCO₃⁻/H₂CO₃, pKₐ 6.1): ~55% of the blood’s buffer capacity; works together with the lungs and kidneys.
  • Hemoglobin (~35%): deoxyhemoglobin binds H⁺ — the Bohr effect.
  • Protein (plasma proteins) and phosphate (HPO₄²⁻/H₂PO₄⁻, pKₐ 6.8), the main buffer inside cells and in urine.

Kidneys

They reabsorb all the filtered HCO₃⁻ and generate new HCO₃⁻ by excreting H⁺ as titratable acids (phosphates) and as ammonium ions NH₄⁺ (from glutamine).

Simplifications

  • Molecules follow their chemical formulas; the number of molecules on screen is arbitrary (proportional to concentration).
  • The buffer beaker is a qualitative model; acid–base values in the disorders are typical examples, and compensation is shown in accelerated time.
